assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a genuinely new physical-chemical concept: condensates form by thermodynamic demixing driven by multivalent weak interactions, giving membraneless compartmentalization. It reframes cell organization in terms of phase behaviour, interfaces and material properties, and has spread across cell biology, neurodegeneration and biophysics. Squarely the kind of soft-matter reduction I value.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granules as liquid droplets (2009), the founding observation; Rosen's multivalent signalling-protein phase transitions (2012) gave the quantitative physical framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence-encoded grammar and could be alternates, so credit is not fully clean, but three names carry the core.
assessment.maturity: Timely: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation and a vast follow-on literature, although the field is still maturing and the in vivo significance of some condensates is debated.
uncertainties: Debate on whether many reported condensates are functional phase separation versus artefacts of overexpression or in vitro conditions.
Whether the discovery is chemistry-appropriate or better seen as physiology/medicine, and how to split credit with Pappu and Mittag.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, and rest on lipid self-assembly, pKa-tuned charge and phase behaviour in the endosome. The impact on medicine is demonstrated at planetary scale, and the underlying science is lipid physical chemistry applied to nucleic-acid encapsulation.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the lipid nanoparticle formulation and ionizable lipid design; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid discovery and screening. Allocation among the Vancouver group and the MIT group is genuinely contested, and several important contributors would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Mature clinically: validated by approved siRNA and mRNA products, though the Nobel in Medicine 2023 recognised the RNA modifications and this chemistry may be viewed as a separate, complementary step.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may make the committee cautious.
Disputed credit across several groups and industrial contributors; can three names fairly represent the invention?

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the funnel concept resolved the Levinthal paradox and gave a statistical-mechanical, thermodynamic foundation for protein folding; it unified folding kinetics, frustration and heterogeneity. A physical-chemical concept of lasting generality, central to how chemists think about biomolecules.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed the funnel/minimal-frustration theory; Dill contributed hydrophobic collapse and lattice models. Fersht provided key experimental phi-value mapping and could be an alternative experimental laureate. The theory trio is defensible, but Dill's role versus Fersht's is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed over three decades, with conceptual influence on structure prediction and design; recognition is arguably overdue for the theory.
uncertainties: Recent protein structure prediction prize (2024) may be seen as covering protein folding already.
Relative credit of Dill, Fersht and Bryngelson.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand cleavage, using engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins; it is a chemical-biology solution to precise genome editing and has already reached clinical trials. Strong originality and clear utility.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab conceived and developed cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as first authors; Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase approach. A single laureate (Liu) is the cleanest configuration, though the parallel Japanese work complicates it.
assessment.maturity: Timely but relatively young: clinical validation is emerging, and long-term safety and off-target profiles remain under study.
uncertainties: Genome editing was recognised in 2020, so a second editing prize may be judged premature.
Priority of the Kondo/Nishida work and the contributions of trainee first authors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity for targeted protein degradation (PROTACs and molecular glues) opens an entirely new pharmacological modality, turning the ubiquitin system into a drug target and making undruggable proteins accessible. High conceptual novelty and rapidly growing impact.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001); Ciulli provided crucial structure-guided VHL ligands and mechanistic insight. The glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto) adds many names; the allocation is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Maturing: multiple compounds in late clinical trials, but no approved PROTAC drug yet; recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: No approved degrader drug as yet.
Fair credit between PROTACs and molecular-glue lineages; Handa/Ito thalidomide mechanism work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods for large biomolecules made solution structure and dynamics, including conformational exchange and sparse states, accessible. Broad and lasting impact on structural and physical biochemistry, and it provides the dynamic view that complements crystallography and cryo-EM.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay are the leading architects of triple-resonance, residual dipolar coupling and TROSY/relaxation-dispersion developments; Wagner and Palmer are also major, so selecting three is a hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, decades of confirmation; NMR was recognised in 1991 and 2002, which may reduce appetite for another NMR prize.
uncertainties: Previous NMR prizes (Ernst, Wuthrich) might make the committee reluctant.
Boundary between method developers when many people contributed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold and related soft lithography provided a simple, general route to molecularly defined interfaces, and underpin surface and colloid chemistry, biointerfaces and microfabrication. A foundational interface concept with extensive reach.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported the alkanethiol-on-gold monolayers (1983); Whitesides greatly extended the field and developed soft lithography. Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority; Xia is mostly for later soft-lithography work.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation; recognition is arguably late and honoring it risks omitting deceased or earlier contributors.
uncertainties: Priority disputes with Sagiv's earlier work.
Whether impact is now seen as established toolkit rather than a current discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules shows how coordination bonds and thermodynamic control give programmable, well-defined supramolecular architectures with host-guest and confined-space chemistry. Conceptually elegant and in line with the logic of molecular self-organization.
assessment.attribution: Fujita's palladium-pyridine cages, Raymond's gallium-catecholate tetrahedra and Stang's coordination-driven self-assembly were independent, comparable contributions; Nitschke and Ward are later extensions. The three-name set is natural.
assessment.maturity: Mature with robust independent confirmation across many groups; supramolecular chemistry was recognised in 1987 and 2016 so novelty vs earlier prizes will be debated.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier supramolecular and MOF-related prizes.
Application impact is less decisive than for other candidates.
